newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia minister says boosting investment is key.
newsitem.headline: Latvia minister says boosting investment is key.

text.p: Latvian Economy Minister Guntar Krasts said on Monday said bringing on new investment to boost GDP growth was one of his key priorities for 1997.

"The policy of attracting investment must be directed at injecting more activity into the whole investment sector -- the state, foreign and the local private sector," Krasts told a news conference on his ministry's plans for 1997.
He noted that the ministry had worked out a development plan for 1998-2000 and that state investment should increase by 50 percent in 1998.
The state investment programme in the 1997 budget is planned at 129.6 million lats, most of which comes from foreign loans.
He noted that privatisation revenues were planned at 32 million lats this year and that the privatisation process was to finish by July 1998.
Krasts also said that Latvia would probably receive more portfolio investment from abroad in 1997 due to lower interest rates and a more active share market rather than foreign direct investment.
He also said that the ministry had much work to do in the energy sector and would formulate a plan to make state energy company Latvenergo more attractive for investment.
Krasts said he hoped that an agreement to sell a stake in Latvenergo to strategic investors would be completed this year.
